title: Days, Weeks, Months & Years
keyIdea: Time comes in sizes. A day is one morning, afternoon, evening and night. Seven days make a week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. About four weeks make a month, and twelve months, from January to December, make a year. The days and the months go round in the same order, so after Sunday comes Monday and after December comes January.

kid: A week has 7 days. They go Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Then the week starts again with Monday.
Today is the day we are in now. Yesterday was the day before. Tomorrow is the day after. If today is Tuesday, yesterday was Monday and tomorrow is Wednesday.
To find the day in 2 days, start on today and hop. The first hop is tomorrow. Do not count today as a hop.
A month is much longer than a week. It is about 4 weeks. There are 12 months in a year. They go from January to December, then a new year starts. Your birthday comes once a year.
adult: England's Year 1 maths programme asks children to 'recognise and use language relating to dates, including days of the week, weeks, months and years', alongside sequencing events in time. Year 2 adds that there are 60 minutes in an hour and 24 hours in a day. The aim at this age is the names in order and how the units nest, not reading a full calendar.

The facts to hold: 7 days in a week, 12 months in a year, 28 to 31 days in a month, 365 days in a year (366 in a leap year), which is 52 weeks and 1 or 2 days. A month is therefore a little over 4 weeks. UK and ISO calendars start the week on Monday, and many US calendars start on Sunday, but the cycle is the same.

Common mistakes: thinking the week ends after Sunday instead of going round, saying 5 days in a week because of school days, mixing up 7 days and 12 months, swapping yesterday and tomorrow, and counting today as the first day when working out 'in 3 days'. Children also often think a month and a week are about the same length.

In the lab your child builds the week wheel and the year wheel by tapping the next name, turns a Today arrow past Sunday, hops on to find a day in a few days, and fills a 30-day April with whole weeks before filling a year with months.

familyTip: Each morning, ask: what day is it today, what was yesterday, and what will tomorrow be? Hang a simple calendar low down and let your child cross off each day. Sing the days of the week or the months while you walk, and count down the days to something exciting by hopping on from tomorrow.

visual.caption: Is it a day of the week or a month? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: build the week wheel, turn past Sunday, hop on to a future day, build the year wheel and fill a month with weeks.

practice.prompt: Today is Wednesday. What day will it be tomorrow?
practice.hint: Tomorrow is the day after today. Say the days in order from Wednesday.
practice.explain: The day after Wednesday is Thursday. Tuesday was yesterday, and Friday is two days away.

practice.prompt: A week has 7 days. You have already had {a} days of this week. How many days of the week are left?
practice.hint: Start from 7 days and take away the days that have gone.
practice.explain: 7 − {a} = {=7-a}, so {=7-a} days of the week are left. Then a new week starts.

practice.prompt: A year has 12 months. {a} months of this year have gone. How many months are left?
practice.hint: Start from 12 months and take away the months that have gone.
practice.explain: 12 − {a} = {=12-a}, so {=12-a} months are left before a new year starts in January.

choices: No day: the week is over
practice.hint: The days go round like a wheel. Where does the week start again?
practice.explain: After Sunday the week starts again, so Monday comes next. Saturday comes before Sunday.

pool.prompt: How many days are in one week?
pool.hint: Say the days from Monday to Sunday and count them on your fingers.
pool.explain: Monday to Sunday is 7 days. School days may be 5, but Saturday and Sunday count too. 12 is the months in a year.

pool.prompt: How many months are in a year?
pool.hint: Say the months from January to December and count them.
pool.explain: January to December is 12 months. 7 is the days in a week, and 52 is about the weeks in a year.

pool.prompt: Today is Saturday. What day was yesterday?
pool.hint: Yesterday is the day just before today.
pool.explain: The day before Saturday is Friday. Sunday is tomorrow, and Thursday was two days ago.

pool.hint: Say the months in order: April, May, June, then what?
pool.explain: July comes straight after June. May comes before June, and August is after July.

pool.prompt: Today is Thursday. What day will it be in 3 days?
pool.hint: Do not count today. Hop: Friday is 1, then keep going.
pool.explain: Friday is 1, Saturday is 2, Sunday is 3. Saturday comes from counting Thursday as 1, and Monday is one hop too many.

pool.prompt: Which is longer: a week or a month?
pool.hint: Think about how many weeks fit in one month.
pool.explain: A month has 28 to 31 days, which is a bit more than 4 weeks. A week is only 7 days.

pool.prompt: A school trip is in {a} weeks. Each week has 7 days. How many days away is the trip?
pool.hint: Each week is 7 days. Count on 7 for each week.
pool.explain: {a} weeks of 7 days is {=a*7} days, so the trip is {=a*7} days away.

pool.prompt: The shop is open {a} days a week. How many days a week is it closed?
pool.hint: A week has 7 days. Take away the days it is open.
pool.explain: 7 − {a} = {=7-a}, so the shop is closed {=7-a} days a week.
